73	func newLoginCmd() *cobra.Command {

75			insecureHTTPAuth bool
76			useDevice        bool
77			server           string
78		)
79		cmd := &cobra.Command{
80			Use:   "login",
81			Short: "Log in to Entire",
82			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {

84				if err != nil {

86				}
87				if err := requireSecureLoginServer(loginServer, insecureHTTPAuth); err != nil {
88					return err
89				}
90				client := auth.NewClient(loginServer, nil, insecureHTTPAuth)
91				// Closure adapts the concrete *auth.BrowserAuthFlow result to the
92				// browserAuthFlow interface (func types are invariant, so the
93				// method value alone won't do). On error the flow is a typed nil,
94				// which is fine — runLoginAuto checks err before touching it.
95				startBrowser := func(ctx context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error) {
96					return client.StartBrowserAuth(ctx)
97				}
98				return runLoginAuto(cmd.Context(), cmd.OutOrStdout(), cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
99					client, startBrowser, openBrowser, loginFlowFacts{
100						useDevice:  useDevice,
101						canPrompt:  interactive.CanPromptInteractively(),
102						sshSession: isSSHSession(),
103					})

107			"login server to authenticate against (rarely needed; the default serves all standard accounts)")
108		addInsecureHTTPAuthFlag(cmd, &insecureHTTPAuth)
109		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&useDevice, "device", false, "Use the device-code flow (enter a code in your browser) instead of the default browser redirect")

113	// parseLoginServer validates and canonicalises the --server value: an
114	// http(s) origin with nothing but scheme and host. Userinfo, path, query,
115	// and fragment are rejected rather than silently dropped — the value
116	// becomes the OAuth issuer, the token-exchange target, and the keyring
117	// key, so surprising rewrites would surface as confusing auth failures
118	// much later. A lone trailing slash is tolerated (normalised away).
119	func parseLoginServer(raw string) (string, error) {
120		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
121		if raw == "" {
122			return "", errors.New("empty server URL")
123		}
124		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
125		if err != nil {
126			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse server URL: %w", err)
127		}
128		// Error messages echo u.Redacted(), not raw: the URL may carry
129		// userinfo (that's one of the rejection cases), and stderr often ends
130		// up in CI logs where a password must not appear.
131		switch {
132		case u.Scheme != schemeHTTPS && u.Scheme != schemeHTTP:
133			return "", fmt.Errorf("scheme must be http or https, got %q", u.Redacted())
134		case u.Host == "":
135			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing host in %q", u.Redacted())
136		case u.User != nil:
137			return "", fmt.Errorf("userinfo not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
138		case u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/":
139			return "", fmt.Errorf("path not allowed in %q (use the bare origin)", u.Redacted())
140		case u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "":
141			return "", fmt.Errorf("query/fragment not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
142		}
143		return api.NormalizeOriginURL(raw), nil
144	}

147	// only host login dials. --insecure-http-auth opts in to http:// (and
148	// enables it process-wide for the token save path).
149	func requireSecureLoginServer(server string, insecureHTTPAuth bool) error {

153		}

160	func runLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, client deviceAuthClient, openURL browserOpenFunc, canPrompt bool) error {
161		start, err := client.StartDeviceAuth(ctx)
162		if err != nil {
163			return fmt.Errorf("start login: %w", err)
164		}
165	
166		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Device code: %s\n", start.UserCode)
167	
168		approvalURL := chooseApprovalURL(start)
169	
170		if canPrompt {
171			// chooseApprovalURL prefers the code-embedded verification_uri_complete,
172			// so opening the URL is usually all the user needs to do. The device
173			// code is printed above regardless, so it's still available to confirm
174			// against the page (RFC 8628 §3.3.1) or to enter on the bare-URI fallback.
175			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Login URL:   %s\n\n", approvalURL)
176			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Press Enter to open in browser...")
177	
178			// Read from /dev/tty so we get a real keypress and don't consume piped stdin.
179			if err := waitForEnter(ctx); err != nil {
180				return fmt.Errorf("wait for input: %w", err)
181			}
182	
183			fmt.Fprintln(outW)
184			if err := openURL(ctx, approvalURL); err != nil {
185				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to open browser: %v\n", err)
186				fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Open this URL in your browser to approve this login: %s\n", approvalURL)
187			}
188		} else {
189			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Login URL:   %s\n\n", approvalURL)
190		}
191	
192		fmt.Fprint(outW, "Waiting for approval... ")
193	
194		token, refreshToken, err := waitForApproval(ctx, client, start.DeviceCode, start.ExpiresIn, time.Duration(start.Interval)*time.Second, defaultSlowDownBackoff)
195		if err != nil {
196			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
197		}
198	
199		return persistLogin(outW, client.BaseURL(), token, refreshToken)
200	}

202	// loginFlowFacts carries the environment facts that pick between the
203	// browser and device-code flows. Detection happens once at the command
204	// entry point; the decision logic below only consumes these values.
205	type loginFlowFacts struct {
206		useDevice  bool // --device flag
207		canPrompt  bool // interactive terminal present
208		sshSession bool // running inside an SSH session
209	}
210	
211	// runLoginAuto picks between the browser (loopback authorization-code) and
212	// device-code flows and runs the chosen one. The browser flow is the
213	// default — no code to type, no poll latency — but it needs a browser that
214	// can reach this machine's 127.0.0.1, so headless terminals (CI, piped
215	// stdin), SSH sessions, and a loopback listener that fails to start all
216	// fall back to the device flow with a one-line explanation; the same
217	// both-flows-with-fallback shape gh / gcloud / aws sso ship. --device
218	// forces the device flow without commentary.
219	func runLoginAuto(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, deviceClient deviceAuthClient, startBrowser func(context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error), openURL browserOpenFunc, facts loginFlowFacts) error {
220		if shouldUseBrowserLogin(facts) {
221			flow, err := startBrowser(ctx)
222			if err != nil {
223				// Binding the loopback listener can fail (sandboxing, firewall,
224				// exhausted ports); that shouldn't strand the user — warn and
225				// use the device flow instead.
226				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: could not start browser sign-in (%v); falling back to the device-code flow.\n", err)
227				return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, openURL, facts.canPrompt)
228			}
229			return runBrowserLogin(ctx, outW, errW, flow, deviceClient.BaseURL(), openURL, browserLoginTimeout)
230		}
231		switch {
232		case facts.useDevice:
233			// Explicitly requested; no explanation needed.
234		case !facts.canPrompt:
235			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "No interactive terminal detected; using device-code flow.")
236		case facts.sshSession:
237			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "SSH session detected; using device-code flow (a browser opened here couldn't reach this machine).")
238		}
239		return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, openURL, facts.canPrompt)
240	}
241	
242	// shouldUseBrowserLogin reports whether `entire login` should use the
243	// loopback authorization-code (browser) flow. The browser flow is the
244	// default but needs a local browser + reachable 127.0.0.1, so it's only
245	// chosen when --device wasn't passed, an interactive terminal is present,
246	// and we're not inside an SSH session (where the loopback listener binds
247	// on the remote host, out of the user's browser's reach); otherwise the
248	// caller falls back to the device flow.
249	func shouldUseBrowserLogin(f loginFlowFacts) bool {
250		return !f.useDevice && f.canPrompt && !f.sshSession
251	}
252	
253	// isSSHSession reports whether this process is running inside an SSH
254	// session: sshd sets SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT for every session and
255	// SSH_TTY for interactive ones.
256	func isSSHSession() bool {
257		return os.Getenv("SSH_CONNECTION") != "" ||
258			os.Getenv("SSH_CLIENT") != "" ||
259			os.Getenv("SSH_TTY") != ""
260	}
261	
262	// runBrowserLogin runs the loopback authorization-code flow on an
263	// already-started flow: open the authorization URL in the user's browser,
264	// wait up to waitTimeout for the redirect back to the local listener, then
265	// exchange the code for tokens. Shares the token validation + persistence
266	// tail with runLogin via persistLogin.
267	func runBrowserLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, flow browserAuthFlow, baseURL string, openURL browserOpenFunc, waitTimeout time.Duration) error {
268		// Wait tears the listener down on return, but Close is idempotent and
269		// covers the error paths before Wait runs.
270		defer func() { _ = flow.Close() }()
271	
272		// Mirror the device flow's interactive shape: show the URL, pause on
273		// Enter before opening the browser, then wait on the same line so
274		// persistLogin's "Login complete." reads "Waiting for sign-in...
275		// Login complete." runBrowserLogin is only reached interactively (see
276		// shouldUseBrowserLogin), so the Enter prompt is unconditional here.
277		authURL := flow.AuthorizationURL()
278		// Show the auth host, not the full authorize URL — the PKCE challenge +
279		// loopback redirect make it long and unreadable, and the browser is
280		// opened for the user anyway. The full URL is only printed below as a
281		// fallback when the browser can't be opened.
282		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Logging in to: %s\n\n", baseURL)
283		fmt.Fprint(outW, "Press Enter to open in browser...")
284	
285		// Read from /dev/tty so we get a real keypress and don't consume piped stdin.
286		if err := waitForEnter(ctx); err != nil {
287			return fmt.Errorf("wait for input: %w", err)
288		}
289		fmt.Fprintln(outW)
290	
291		if err := openURL(ctx, authURL); err != nil {
292			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to open browser: %v\n", err)
293			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Open this URL in your browser to sign in: %s\n", authURL)
294		}
295	
296		fmt.Fprint(outW, "Waiting for sign-in... ")
297	
298		// The clock starts here, after the Enter prompt, so time spent reading
299		// the prompt isn't counted against the sign-in itself.
300		waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, waitTimeout)
301		defer cancel()
302	
303		code, err := flow.Wait(waitCtx)
304		if err != nil {
305			if errors.Is(waitCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
306				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for sign-in after %v; run `entire login` again, or use `entire login --device`", waitTimeout)
307			}
308			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
309		}
310	
311		token, refreshToken, err := flow.Exchange(ctx, code)
312		if err != nil {
313			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
314		}
315	
316		return persistLogin(outW, baseURL, token, refreshToken)
317	}

319	// persistLogin validates the freshly-issued access token and records it in
320	// the shared contexts.json credential model. Shared by the device-code and
321	// browser flows.
322	func persistLogin(outW io.Writer, baseURL, token, refreshToken string) error {
323		if err := validateReceivedToken(token, baseURL, time.Now()); err != nil {
324			return fmt.Errorf("reject login token: %w", err)
325		}
326	
327		// Record the login in the shared contexts.json credential model — the
328		// single store every consumer (control plane, data API, git remote
329		// helper, entiredb's CLIs) resolves against.
330		if _, err := auth.RecordLoginContext(token, refreshToken, true); err != nil {
331			return fmt.Errorf("save login: %w", withHeadlessStoreHint(err))
332		}
333	
334		fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Login complete.")
335		return nil
336	}
337	
338	// withHeadlessStoreHint appends file-token-store guidance to a credential
339	// store write failure. The default backend is the OS keyring, which locked
340	// or keyring-less machines (CI, containers, minimal server VMs) can't use —
341	// the raw store error gives those users no way forward (#1036). The hint is
342	// skipped when ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file is already set (suggesting it again
343	// would be nonsense) and for failures the file store wouldn't help with.
344	func withHeadlessStoreHint(err error) error {
345		if !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrCredentialStoreWrite) || tokenstore.FileBackendSelected() {
346			return err
347		}
348	
349		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nIf this machine has no usable OS keyring (headless server, container, CI), store tokens in a file instead:\n\n  %s=file entire login\n\nTokens are then written with 0600 permissions to %s (override the location with %s)",
350			err, tokenstore.BackendEnvVar, tokenstore.FileBackendPath(), tokenstore.PathEnvVar)
351	}
352	
353	// validateReceivedToken runs minimum-trust checks on the access token
354	// the AS handed us before we persist it. The server is the authority
355	// on signature/exp; this is defense in depth aimed at catching gross
356	// misbehaviour by a compromised or misconfigured AS (e.g. handing back
357	// a token from a different issuer than the one we asked, or one whose
358	// claims are already-expired).
359	//
360	// It also enforces what the contexts model needs up front:
361	// RecordLoginContext — the sole persistence path — keys the context and
362	// keychain slot on the token's iss and handle/sub claims, so a token
363	// without parseable claims can never complete a login. Rejecting it here
364	// names the requirement instead of surfacing a parse error from the save
365	// step. Entire-core always issues claim-bearing JWTs; opaque-token-only
366	// servers are not supported.
367	func validateReceivedToken(rawToken, issuerURL string, now time.Time) error {
368		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(rawToken)
369		if errors.Is(err, tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT) {
370			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // sentinel surfaces verbatim for caller's errors.Is
371		}
372		if err != nil {
373			return fmt.Errorf("login server issued a token without parseable JWT claims (claim-bearing JWTs are required): %w", err)
374		}
375		if claims.Issuer == "" {
376			return errors.New("token has no iss claim; cannot record a login context")
377		}
378		if claims.Handle == "" && claims.Subject == "" {
379			return errors.New("token has no handle or sub claim; cannot record a login context")
380		}
381	
382		// iss check: the token must claim to come from the issuer we sent
383		// the device-code request to. A mismatch means either the AS is
384		// misconfigured or someone's playing games.
385		if issErr := issMatches(claims.Issuer, issuerURL); issErr != nil {
386			return issErr
387		}
388	
389		// exp sanity: a token that's already expired before we even store
390		// it is a smell. Don't reject if exp is unset (some servers omit).
391		if !claims.ExpiresAt.IsZero() && !now.Before(claims.ExpiresAt) {
392			return fmt.Errorf("token already expired (exp=%s, now=%s)",
393				claims.ExpiresAt.Format(time.RFC3339), now.Format(time.RFC3339))
394		}
395	
396		return nil
397	}
398	
399	// issMatches reports whether claimed equals expected after stripping path/
400	// query/fragment via api.OriginOnly, so "https://issuer/" and "https://issuer"
401	// match. The caller has already rejected an empty iss claim.
402	func issMatches(claimed, expected string) error {
403		normClaimed := api.OriginOnly(claimed)
404		normExpected := api.OriginOnly(expected)
405		if normClaimed != normExpected {
406			return fmt.Errorf("iss mismatch: token claims %q, expected %q", normClaimed, normExpected)
407		}
408		return nil
409	}

411	func waitForApproval(ctx context.Context, poller deviceAuthClient, deviceCode string, expiresIn int, interval, slowDownBackoff time.Duration) (accessToken, refreshToken string, err error) {
412		expiry := time.Duration(expiresIn) * time.Second
413		if expiry <= 0 || expiry > maxExpiresIn {
414			expiry = maxExpiresIn
415		}
416		deadline := time.Now().Add(expiry)
417		pollInterval := interval
418		if pollInterval <= 0 {
419			pollInterval = fallbackDeviceAuthPollInterval
420		}
421	
422		consecutiveErrors := 0
423	
424		for {
425			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
426				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
427			}
428	
429			result, err := poller.PollDeviceAuth(ctx, deviceCode)
430			if err != nil {
431				consecutiveErrors++
432				if consecutiveErrors >= maxTransientErrors {
433					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("poll approval status (after %d consecutive failures): %w", consecutiveErrors, err)
434				}
435				// Transient error — wait and retry.
436				select {
437				case <-ctx.Done():
438					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
439				case <-time.After(pollInterval):
440				}
441				continue
442			}
443			consecutiveErrors = 0
444	
445			switch result.Error {
446			case "":
447				if result.AccessToken == "" {
448					return "", "", errors.New("device authorization completed without a token")
449				}
450				return result.AccessToken, result.RefreshToken, nil
451			case "authorization_pending":
452				// no-op, will sleep and retry below
453			case "slow_down":
454				pollInterval += slowDownBackoff
455				if pollInterval > maxPollInterval {
456					pollInterval = maxPollInterval
457				}
458			case "access_denied":
459				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization denied")
460			case "expired_token":
461				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")

gh pr create --title "fix: hint CLI update command on cli_upgrade_required errors" --body "## Problem

\`entire login\` against a server that requires a newer CLI failed with only the raw OAuth code:

\`\`\`
start login: start device auth: cli_upgrade_required
\`\`\`

No way forward for the user — while the periodic version check (plain \`entire\`) does show the update command.

## Fix

Append the install-manager-aware update command (from \`versioncheck.UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary\`, the same one the version check advertises) whenever a command error carries \`cli_upgrade_required\`:

\`\`\`
start login: start device auth: oauth error: cli_upgrade_required

This version of the Entire CLI is too old for this server. Update it, then rerun the command:

  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
\`\`\`

## Why main.go, not login

The code can surface from any auth-server OAuth flow — auth-go emits the same error string from \`deviceflow\`, \`authcode\`, \`refresh\`, and \`sts\`. That means not just login, but the refresh grant under nearly every authenticated command and the RFC 8693 exchanges (jurisdiction/cell tokens). \`main.go\`'s default error-print arm is the repo's documented single choke point for command errors (root sets \`SilenceErrors\`, main prints), so one \`cli.WithCLIUpgradeHint(err)\` there covers all of them.

Detection is a string match on the code — auth-go exposes no sentinel for unrecognised OAuth codes.

Known gaps (accepted): \`SilentError\` paths bypass the printer (they print curated messages, not raw OAuth codes); \`git-remote-entire\` is a separate binary and would need the same one-liner if the server ever gates repo-creds exchange.

## Testing

- Unit tests for \`WithCLIUpgradeHint\` (login-shaped and refresh-shaped errors, pass-through, nil)
- \`mise run test:ci\` green (unit + integration + e2e canary)
- Verified end-to-end: real binary against a fake AS returning \`cli_upgrade_required\` prints the hint above
